{"criterion": "Reported earnings convert to cash across every period in the bundle, with no recurring non-GAAP add-back and no accounting-policy change in the window.", "why": "STEP 1 — the cash test, to the extent the bundle permits it.

(1) FACT [10-Q:0000723125-25-000021, Consolidated Statements of Operations]: "Net income (loss) | $1,885 | $332 | $5,338 | $(109)" — i.e. $5,338M for the nine months ended May 29, 2025 and $(109)M for the nine months ended May 30, 2024.
(2) FACT [10-Q:0000723125-25-000021, Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows]: "Net cash provided by operating activities | 11,795 | 5,102".
(3) INFERENCE [from 1, 2]: In both periods for which the bundle reports cash flow, operating cash flow exceeded net income — by a wide margin in FY25 nine months, and in FY24 nine months operating cash inflow of $5,102M was reported against a reported net loss. There is no period in the bundle where reported earnings exceed reported operating cash flow.
(4) FACT [same statement]: the reconciling add-backs are "Depreciation expense and amortization of intangible assets | 6,203 | 5,794" and "Stock-based compensation | 722 | 620".
(5) FACT [same statement, change in operating assets and liabilities, FY25 9M vs FY24 9M]: "Receivables | (123) | (2,562)"; "Inventories | 148 | (125)"; "Other current assets (206) | (435)"; "Accounts payable and accrued expenses | 38 | 846"; "Other current liabilities (681) | 769"; "Other | 356 | 304".
(6) INFERENCE [from 1, 2, 4, 5]: The gap between operating cash flow and net income in FY25 nine months is driven by depreciation and amortization, not by working-capital release; working capital in aggregate was a modest net drag (receivables, other current assets and other current liabilities were uses of cash, inventories and payables small sources). The conversion is therefore explained by the capital intensity of the asset base rather than by accrual timing.
(7) DATA GAP: the bundle contains no <computed_metrics> block. The accrual ratio (STEP 1b), free cash flow against net income (STEP 1c), days sales outstanding / days inventory / days payable (STEP 3), the ROE decomposition into margin, turnover and leverage (STEP 4), and stock-based compensation as a share of revenue (STEP 2c) are not supplied in pre-computed form, and I am not permitted to derive them. Those four tests are therefore unperformed, not passed.
(8) FACT [Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows]: "Expenditures for property, plant, and equipment | (10,199) | (5,266)" and "Proceeds from government incentives | 1,294 | 267".
(9) INFERENCE [from 2, 4, 8]: Capital expenditure of $10,199M in the FY25 nine months is of the same order as operating cash flow of $11,795M and larger than the $6,203M depreciation and amortization charge, so cash remaining after all capital expenditure is a small fraction of operating cash flow and is not obviously larger than net income. The bundle does not supply the free-cash-flow figure or its ratio to net income, so I state the magnitudes and stop. This is the material qualification on "cash the owners could have": the cash is being generated and reinvested, and the bundle shows no buybacks — FACT [Equity note]: "No shares were repurchased in the first nine months of 2025" — with FACT [Cash Flows]: "Payments of dividends to shareholders | (392) | (384)".
(10) DATA GAP: cash flow is reported only for the two nine-month periods. The bundle reports quarterly net income for Q3 FY25, Q2 FY25 and Q3 FY24 (FACT [MD&A Consolidated Results]: "Net income (loss) | $1,885 | 20% | $1,583 | 20% | $332 | 5% | $5,338 | 20% | $(109) | (1)%") with no matching quarterly operating cash flow. Per-quarter conversion is therefore unchecked rather than verified; nothing in the bundle indicates it was uneven.

STEP 2 — composition.

(11) FACT [E-04, ng.measure, status not_found]: "Searched the full 10-Q: no non-GAAP measure is presented. EBITDA appears only in the definitions table of commonly used terms, and 'adjusted EBITDA' only as a covenant term in the Term Loan Agreement discussion; neither is presented as a reported non-GAAP measure."
(12) FACT [E-04, ng.adjustment, status not_found]: "The only reconciling lines in the filing are the ASC 280 'Unallocated' items reconciling total segment operating income to GAAP total operating income — a GAAP segment reconciliation, not adjustments to a non-GAAP measure. No non-GAAP adjustment schedule exists in the document."
(13) FACT [E-04, ng.nongaap_end, status not_found]: "No resulting non-GAAP figure is presented anywhere in the 10-Q; the statements of operations, MD&A results tables and notes report GAAP measures only."
(14) INFERENCE [from 11, 12, 13]: There is no adjusted earnings figure in this window, so there is no recurring non-GAAP add-back on which reported earnings could depend. The headline figure being assessed is GAAP net income.
(15) FACT [Segment and Other Information note, Unallocated block, columns Q3 FY25 | Q3 FY24 | 9M FY25 | 9M FY24]: "Stock-based compensation | (263) | (217) | (713) | (608)"; "Patent license charges | (57) | — | (57) | —"; "Lower costs from sale of inventory written down in prior periods | — | — | — | 987"; "Patent cross-license agreement gain | — | — | — | 200"; "Other | (1) | (5) | (5) | —".
(16) FACT [seg.op_income]: total segment operating income "2,490 | 941 | 6,891 | (797)" reconciles to "Total operating income (loss) $2,169 | $719 | $6,116 | $(218)".
(17) INFERENCE [from 15, 16]: Stock-based compensation is excluded from the segment profit measure in all four columns, so if the segment measure were treated as the headline figure there would be a recurring exclusion. It is not the headline figure: GAAP total operating income and GAAP net income are reported on the face of the statements (1), the segment exclusion is the ASC 280 presentation (12), and the note states a basis for non-allocation — FACT [Segment note]: "nor do we allocate gains and losses from equity method investments, interest, other non-operating income or expense items, or taxes to segments."
(18) INFERENCE [from 15]: The two large non-operating benefits in the bundle sit in the FY24 comparative, not in FY25: the $987M inventory-writedown-reversal benefit and the $200M patent cross-license gain. FACT [MD&A Consolidated Gross Margin]: "Our consolidated gross margin for the first nine months of 2024 reflected $987 million of benefit due to lower costs from the sale of inventories written down to their net realizable value in 2023." Their absence from FY25 means the FY25 improvement is not attributable to them; it also means the FY24 base was flattered.
(19) FACT [Income Taxes note]: "The effect of tax incentive arrangements reduced our tax provision by $240 million (benefiting our diluted earnings per share by $0.21) and $623 million (benefiting our diluted earnings per share by $0.55) for the third quarter and first nine months of 2025"; and "Effective tax rate 11.1% | 52.7% | 11.5% | 63.7%".
(20) FACT [Income Taxes note]: "On November 27, 2024, Singapore enacted legislation to implement Pillar Two, which will apply to us starting in 2026. While we are still evaluating the impacts, we expect our effective tax rate for 2026 to be in the high-teens percentage range."
(21) INFERENCE [from 19, 20]: A disclosed and quantified part of FY25 earnings is a conditional tax incentive, not operating performance; the filing itself states the conditionality — FACT: "These incentives expire, in whole or in part, at various dates through 2034 and are conditional, in part, upon meeting certain business operations and employment thresholds." This is a durability question about the tax line, not an accrual-quality or cash-conversion defect, since tax incentives reduce cash taxes as well as the provision — though the bundle does not disclose cash taxes paid, so that last point is a gap.
(22) FACT [Debt note]: "In the third quarter of 2025, we recognized a $46 million loss in other non-operating income (expense) on prepayment of the 2027 Notes." FACT [Derivatives note]: "We recognized gains of $106 million and $38 million for derivative instruments without hedge accounting designation for the third quarter and first nine months of 2025"; and "We recognized losses of $93 million and gains of $52 million for the third quarter and first nine months of 2025... and offsetting gains of $93 million and losses of $46 million... for changes in the underlying fair values of the hedged items".
(23) INFERENCE [from 22]: Fair-value marks in the quarter are disclosed and largely offsetting within other non-operating income (expense), which was $(68)M for the quarter against operating income of $2,169M — FACT [Statements of Operations]: "Other non-operating income (expense), net | (68) | 10 | (90) | (24)"; "Operating income (loss) | 2,169 | 719 | 6,116 | (218)". These items are small relative to operating income and run in the loss direction in FY25, so they are not propping up the figure.
(24) FACT [Revenue and Customer Contract Liabilities note]: "customer prepayments made to secure product supply in future periods and other contract liabilities were $146 million and $907 million, respectively" and "Revenue recognized during the first nine months of 2025 from the beginning balance as of August 29, 2024 included $777 million from shipments against customer prepayments and other contract liabilities."
(25) INFERENCE [from 5, 24]: $777M of FY25 nine-month revenue was recognised against cash collected in an earlier period, which is consistent with the $(681)M use of cash in "Other current liabilities" in the FY25 operating cash flow. That is revenue whose cash arrived earlier, not revenue whose cash has yet to arrive; it lowers current-period cash conversion rather than inflating it.
(26) FACT [SBC note]: "Stock-based compensation expense by caption... $263 | $217 | $713 | $608", and "Stock-based compensation expense of $109 million and $99 million was capitalized and remained in inventory as of May 29, 2025 and August 29, 2024, respectively." FACT [Statements of Operations]: "Revenue | $9,301 | $6,811 | $26,063 | $17,361". DATA GAP: the SBC-to-revenue ratio and its trend are not supplied pre-computed, so I record the levels and do not state a trend in percentage terms.

STEP 3 — working capital, to the extent the bundle permits.

(27) DATA GAP: DSO, days inventory and days payable are not supplied for any period. The formal STEP 3 test cannot be run.
(28) FACT [Receivables note]: "Trade receivables | $5,492 | $5,419"; "Government incentives 1,320 | 834"; total "$7,436 | $6,615". FACT [Inventories note]: total "$8,727 | $8,875". FACT [Statements of Operations]: "Cost of goods sold | 5,793 | 4,979 | 16,244 | 14,485".
(29) INFERENCE [from 28 and revenue in 26]: Trade receivables were close to flat between August 29, 2024 and May 29, 2025 while nine-month revenue was substantially higher year over year, and the increase in total receivables is concentrated in the government-incentives line rather than in amounts owed by customers; inventories declined while nine-month cost of goods sold was higher year over year. Neither of the two classic borrowing-from-the-future patterns (receivables outrunning revenue, inventory outrunning cost of sales) is visible in the balances the bundle gives. Without the days metrics this is a directional observation on balances, not a measured result.

STEP 4 — return decomposition.

(30) DATA GAP: no ROE figure, no margin/turnover/leverage decomposition and no return series are supplied. FACT [Balance Sheets]: "Total equity | 50,748 | 45,131"; "Total liabilities | 27,649 | 24,285"; "Total assets | $78,397 | $69,416"; FACT [Debt note]: "$538 | $15,003 | $15,541 | $431 | $12,966 | $13,397". INFERENCE [from these and 1]: both equity and debt carrying value rose over the nine months, so I cannot attribute any change in return on equity to margin versus leverage — the decomposition is unavailable and I decline to infer it from balances. The margin move itself is given: FACT [MD&A]: "Gross margin | 3,508 | 38% | 2,963 | 37% | 1,832 | 27% | 9,819 | 38% | 2,876 | 17%".

Accounting-policy test.

(31) FACT [E-09, ap.change, status not_found]: "Checked Significant Accounting Policies note and Critical Accounting Estimates in MD&A; both state no changes. — There have been no changes to our significant accounting policies since our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended August 29, 2024."
(32) FACT [E-09, ap.useful_life / ap.reserve / ap.capitalisation, all status not_found]: no change in useful lives, reserve methodology or capitalisation policy is disclosed; e.g. "Checked Intangible Assets and Property, Plant, and Equipment notes; lives stated but no change disclosed."
(33) FACT [E-09, ap.change, status found, qualifier "Prior-period reclassifications", note "No reason or quantified effect given."]: "Certain reclassifications have been made to prior-period amounts to conform to current-period presentation."
(34) FACT [E-09, ap.change, status found, qualifier "Segment structure reorganization"]: "We completed reorganization of our operations and organizational structure and began to manage operations under our new segment structure effective in the fourth quarter of 2025", and [seg.basis_note]: "The changes will require us to recast our segment reporting and we will report financial results under this new structure starting with our 2025 Annual Report on Form 10-K."
(35) INFERENCE [from 31, 32, 33, 34]: The two "found" items are presentation matters outside the measurement of this window's earnings — an unquantified prior-period reclassification, and a segment recast that takes effect in Q4 FY25 and will first appear in the 10-K. Against the explicit statement that no significant accounting policy changed (31) and no change in lives, reserves or capitalisation (32), I read the window as containing no accounting-policy change that moved reported earnings. The reclassification is the weak point: the bundle gives neither its reason nor its effect (33), so this reading rests on the absence of a disclosed effect rather than on a disclosed zero.
(36) FACT [E-09, ap.icfr, status not_found]: "Item 4 Controls and Procedures: controls concluded effective; no material weakness or significant deficiency disclosed." FACT [E-09, ap.auditor, status not_found]: no auditor change or modified opinion; the statements are unaudited interim statements.
(37) FACT [seg.basis_note]: "Segment information reported herein is consistent with how it was reviewed and evaluated by our chief operating decision maker for the applicable time periods", and [seg.basis_note]: "Single basis presented: the four-unit CNBU/SBU/MBU/EBU structure, as originally reported. No restated segment figures appear in this filing."

Why this criterion and not the adjacent ones.

(38) INFERENCE [from 14]: the option describing "non-GAAP add-backs that are disclosed, non-recurring and individually explained" presupposes add-backs that exist; the bundle's targeted search found none, so that option's stated requirement is not met by the evidence.
(39) INFERENCE [from 3, 10, 29]: the option requiring conversion to be "uneven across the bundle's periods" is unavailable — in both cash-flow periods operating cash flow exceeded net income, and no quarterly cash flow statement exists to show unevenness. Choosing it would require me to treat a data gap as a finding.
(40) INFERENCE [from 14, 35]: the option requiring dependence on recurring add-backs or an in-window accounting-policy change is unavailable — there is no non-GAAP measure at all, and the only policy-adjacent disclosures are an unquantified reclassification and a recast effective after this window.
(41) INFERENCE [from 2, 3]: the option stating the bundle does not permit a cash-conversion assessment overstates the gap — the face of the cash flow statement puts operating cash flow beside net income for two periods, which is a conversion assessment, even though the accrual ratio, FCF ratio, working-capital days and ROE decomposition are all missing (7, 27, 30).
(42) INFERENCE [from 7, 10, 21, 30]: the selected criterion is satisfied on its own terms — conversion holds in every period the bundle measures, no recurring non-GAAP add-back exists, no accounting-policy change moved the figure — but the reader should weigh it knowing that four of the six quantitative tests requested could not be run, that per-quarter conversion is unchecked, that cash after $10,199M of capital expenditure is a much smaller number than the $11,795M operating cash flow, and that $623M of the nine-month figure comes from conditional tax incentives.", "what_would_move_it_down": "A quarterly statement of cash flows showing operating cash flow below net income in any single quarter of this window — Q3 FY25, Q2 FY25 or Q3 FY24 — would make conversion uneven across the bundle's periods and move me to "Conversion is uneven across the bundle's periods, or add-backs recur without a stated reason.""}
